sources_read: .qc-cache/kittle-2026-10-09-r6/rules/WebDev Rubrics QC.xlsx :: Quality Checks row 26 (#25) and Internal Quality Checks row 26 (#25; no extra annotation cells)
evidence: All five prompts open with 'Evaluate the live application at http://localhost:3000 using Playwright MCP' (gates/render/prompt.md:1, gates/constraints/prompt.md:1, scored/functional/prompt.md:1, scored/polish/prompt.md:1; scored/visual/prompt.md:1-2 'Evaluate the rendered application at http://localhost:3000 using Playwright MCP'), and every judge.toml declares the playwright stdio MCP server (playwright-mcp --headless --isolated, chromium); functional additionally wires the verifier restart server. Each prompt restricts evidence to the browser: render:2 'Use only rendered browser behavior', constraints:2 'browser-visible behavior and browser network evidence only', polish:4 'Judge the rendered product and interactions, not code style', visual:22 'Score each criterion independently from rendered evidence', functional:23-28 'passes only on evidence you gathered in this session... A step you skipped... fails', functional:46-47 'Never use curl or shell commands', and all treat submitted source as untrusted. First-paint guesses are excluded: functional/polish/visual gates (functional:11-19, polish:10-18, visual:18-26) say 'a first-paint imitation does not pass' and require sign-in plus server-backed data; the constraints gate (judge.toml) posts a message, reloads and re-reads it from a second browser context; every functional/polish criterion is a scripted interaction sequence (post/reload/replay/escape/resize) and visual criteria require navigating to M-11, M-13, the transcript and a 390x844 resize (visual prompt:49). app_context.md is injected into each {app_context} (test.sh:197-201) and supplies only URL/accounts/browser-context how-tos, no expected answers that permit memory-based scoring. Counterexample attempts: a static shell with plausible source fails the render/constraints gates (sign-in rejection, cross-context persistence); a conforming SPA with different routes/labels is protected by 'Judge observable outcomes rather than exact wording or selectors' and 'Any endpoint path... is acceptable'. Prompt preambles match the frozen template apart from task-added gate/state text. Note (not a defect of this row): no full configured judge run exists for these bytes (raw-evidence-index scope), so actual judge tool use is NOT EXERCISED; this row's procedure is a prompt-content check, and the prompts satisfy it.
